text: The matrix and conflict versions resolve at sign-in and stay with the session until it ends, and the resolved role set, scope and the two version labels are handed to gateway-bff for its Redis session record while rwb-access keeps no session table of its own.
why: The legacy story kept the versions on the session object and refused to change them under an open session, and the target forbids a session table and a token store in a service; without a stated home the AC9 behaviour cannot be built.
read: RWB-E1-022 section 8 BR7 and section 13 build step 8; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 (gateway-bff: Redis sessions only) and 35; ADR-010; RWB-PLT-N006-INF
confirm: rwb-access service owner and the edge owner at the wave 1 design gate
impact: Decides where the version labels live; adds no table, no column and no schema to rwb_access and keeps the sessions in the edge store

text: A role conflict refuses the session with MSG-P4-006 naming the pair, and the refusal and the incident it raises are one refusal fact with reason code ROLE_CONFLICT.
why: The legacy criterion requires an incident on the security administrator queue, and no source of the read set names an incident operation, a queue or a target service, so the refusal fact is the only channel that exists.
read: RWB-E1-022 section 5 X4 and section 7 AC6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 publishes no event); RWB-P4-E1039-APP's access-entry writer
confirm: Security administrator role owner and the audit owner at the wave 1 design gate
impact: Gives the incident an addressee through the record that already exists; a dedicated incident operation would be a new contract and is not created

text: An unmapped or inactive group gives no role, and its name is written on the sign-in fact as a group name only, never as a person's attribute.
why: The ownership and the FSD agree that a group with no active role row confers nothing, and the legacy criterion also requires the unmapped name to be visible, so the fact must carry a name whose kind has to be fixed to keep personal data out.
read: RWB-E1-022 section 5 X6, section 8 BR1 and section 7 AC8; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-04; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 35
confirm: rwb-access service owner at the wave 1 design gate
impact: The fact carries a group name and a reference; no person attribute reaches a log or an event

text: rwb-access caches nothing of another service's data: the reference values and the team and region codes are read per call through the rwb-case contracts, and no row is copied into rwb_access.
why: The reference lists and the teams are P3's under the ownership map, and a copy in rwb_access would be a second source that drifts at the first version change; the schema story states that no object of rwb_access references rwb_case.
read: Ownership Map v1 (lov_value, reference_row, reference_version, queue, queue_member owned by P3); DP-01 and DP-07; RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON; RWB-P3-E1019-CON
confirm: rwb-access service owner and the rwb-case service owner at the wave 1 contract freeze
impact: One hop per resolution for the values and the team codes; no local copy, no local invalidation and no drift

text: The sign-in and refusal facts are written locally by the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP and published to rwb.decision-record.v1; this story supplies the reference, the area, the right, the result and the reason code and builds no writer of its own.
why: The access log is written locally and published to the decision topic, and the writer is one story of this service; a second writer inside the resolver would duplicate the record path and the hash chain.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 (every service writes its own decision records) and 22; DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; RWB-E1-022 section 13 build step 5
confirm: rwb-access service owner and the audit owner at the wave 1 design gate
impact: One record path for every refusal and sign-in; the resolver adds no writer, no table and no topic

text: The two operations of the access contract are published at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions, built from the operation names of Architecture v5 slide 14 and the base rule of section R4.
why: The slide names the operations and the Ownership Map has no path row for either, so the base rule is the only published derivation of a path; leaving it open would leave every consumer guessing the same two strings.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Template and Rules section R4 and DP-13; Ownership Map v1 api list (no row for authorise or me/permissions)
confirm: Contract owner of rwb-access and the platform edge owner at the contract freeze
impact: Fixes two paths and no payload; a later Ownership Map path row would replace the assumption and not the operations

text: The authorise request carries the role codes of the resolved session, the scope type with the team and region codes, the capability area, the right and the delegation band key of the action, and the answer carries the decision, the matrix version, the conflict version and on a refusal the reason code and the message id.
why: No source fixes the payload: the legacy contract was a Java method over a SessionContext type and the slide names only the inputs role, scope and DoA, so the contract must state the shape it publishes and say that it is stated.
read: RWB-E1-022 section 12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (POST /authorise: role, scope, DoA) and slide 11 (REST, one hop, 2 s); TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-012 (the resolved session holds roles, scope, matrix and conflict versions)
applied_in: RWB-P4-E1022-CON sections 4, 7 AC2 and AC3, and 12.1
confirm: Contract owner of rwb-access with the consuming squads at the contract freeze
impact: Fixes the shape every consumer compiles against; it carries identifiers and version labels only and no business value

text: The grantee of schema rwb_access is a login named rwb_access, following the one-login-per-service pattern of section R4 and Architecture v5 slide 29, and the platform DB story sets its real name, its password and its connection pool.
why: Section R4 fixes one login per service and no source fixes the P4 login name; the grant script, the boundary check and the rollback all need a named grantee to be testable.
read: Template and Rules section R4 (login per service); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 (one login per service, rwb_case shown as the pattern); RWB-PLT-N011-DB (pools, migrator role and grant check)
applied_in: RWB-P4-E1022-DB sections 3, 7 AC1 and AC7, 13 and 17
confirm: ACE DBA and the platform DB owner at the wave 1 schema gate
impact: Names the grantee of the script only; no credential appears in a migration, a story or a runbook

text: The role-to-group mapping rows stay in role.entra_group as TSD P4 v3 defines them, the ACE group facts behind a mapping are read only through the P1 contract or RWB-P1-E1069-APP, and no object of rwb_access names an ACE schema, the recovery schema or public.
why: FSD P4 v3 reads the mapping from v_ace_iam_group while TSD P4 v3 defines role.entra_group and the mapping contract keeps the rows in the table; R-PREC puts the technical specification above the functional one, and the boundary rule forbids a service reading ACE directly.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.1 field catalog; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role (DF-REF-039); Template and Rules section R3 R-PREC items 6 and 7; Ownership Map v1 role row; RWB-P1-E1069-APP (the ACE view owner)
confirm: P4 service owner, the P1 data owner and the architecture review at the wave 1 schema gate
impact: Keeps one mapping row set in rwb_access and one read path for the ACE facts; no view, synonym or grant crosses the schema boundary

text: outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key are created in rwb_access from the event platform template published by RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, unchanged, by this service's own database story.
why: The ownership map keeps the three objects with PLT as library objects created in every service schema and Architecture v5 slide 29 forbids a cross-schema write, so this schema must hold them before the service can publish or consume idempotently.
read: Ownership Map v1 rows outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key (owner PLT, asm ASM-A6-tables-8); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 20; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON
confirm: ACE DBA and the event platform owner at the wave 1 schema gate
impact: The three objects are applied from one template and no column is invented here; a template change is one change in one place
